text: Agents are generically typed by dependency and output types, giving IDE type-checking support
quote: agents are generic in their dependency and output types, e.g., an agent which required dependencies of type Foobar and produced outputs of type list[str] would have type Agent[Foobar, list[str]]

text: Model-agnostic framework with built-in support for many different LLM providers, swap models via a string
quote: a typed, extensible agent loop with every model a string swap away

text: Many other providers can be used via an OpenAI-API-compatible model class
quote: many providers are compatible with the OpenAI API, and can be used with OpenAIChatModel in Pydantic AI

text: The same agent object can run behind a web frontend, in a terminal, on a voice call, or on a durable background queue
quote: The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue, or as a plain object you call run() on.

text: Ships a complete terminal coding agent with workspace-scoped file access, allowlisted shell, repo orientation and planning
quote: A complete coding agent in your terminal: workspace-rooted file access, allowlisted shell, repo orientation, planning, and context management that survives long sessions.

text: Function tools let models perform actions and retrieve extra info to help generate a response
quote: Function tools provide a mechanism for models to perform actions and retrieve extra information to help them generate a response.

text: Can force model output to match a Pydantic model schema for structured output
quote: Here's an example using a Pydantic model as the `output_type`, forcing the model to respond with data matching our specification

text: Provides access to full message history from an agent run for continuing conversations or analysis
quote: Pydantic AI provides access to messages exchanged during an agent run. These messages can be used both to continue a coherent conversation, and to understand how an agent performed.

text: Can act as an MCP client, connecting to MCP servers to use their tools within an agent run
quote: Pydantic AI can act as an MCP client, connecting to MCP servers to use their tools as part of an agent run.

text: Supports agent delegation where one agent delegates work to another agent and resumes control after completion
quote: "Agent delegation" refers to the scenario where an agent delegates work to another agent, then takes back control when the delegate agent ... finishes.

text: Supports durable agents that preserve progress across transient API failures, errors, or restarts
quote: Pydantic AI allows you to build durable agents that can preserve their progress across transient API failures and application errors or restarts

text: Tool calls may require human approval before execution
quote: it may need to be approved by the user first

text: Pydantic Evals is a code-first framework for systematically testing and evaluating AI systems, from single calls to multi-agent apps
quote: Pydantic Evals is a powerful evaluation framework for systematically testing and evaluating AI systems, from simple LLM calls to complex multi-agent applications.

text: Generates traces and spans for each model request and tool call during an agent run
quote: A trace is generated for the agent run, and spans are emitted for each model request and tool call.

text: Includes an official CLI (clai) for chatting with LLMs and getting quick answers from the command line
quote: Pydantic AI comes with a CLI, `clai` ... You can use it to chat with various LLMs and quickly get answers, right from the command line

text: Can launch CLI mode directly from an Agent instance via to_cli_sync()
quote: you can directly launch CLI mode from an `Agent` instance using `Agent.to_cli_sync()`

text: Supports tool calls that shouldn't or can't be executed within the same agent run/process, enabling human-in-the-loop workflows
quote: There are a few scenarios where the model should be able to call a tool that should not or cannot be executed during the same agent run inside the same Python process

text: Built-in optional integration with Logfire sends detailed agent run information for observability
quote: Pydantic AI has built-in (but optional) support for Logfire...detailed information about agent runs is sent to Logfire.

text: @agent.tool decorator gives tools access to agent context by default
quote: @agent.tool is considered the default decorator since in the majority of cases tools will need access to the agent context.

text: Provides TestModel and FunctionModel for testing and development with mocked models
quote: Pydantic AI also comes with TestModel and FunctionModel for testing and development.
